keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 194-214; Cliopatria has no row and the Han shape (han-dynasty_184 to 215) keeps Hanzhong inside. The Celestial Masters page: the 'theocratic state of Zhang Han in the Hanzhong Valley', independent from 194; the Battle of Yangping page names Hanzhong Commandery (capital Nanzheng) and gives no extent, so a 100 km circle at Hanzhong stands for it. Reviewer fix (ea-02-x-fixed): the Guangyuan 80 km circle (a stand-in for Bazhong) is gone from 194-214. The Yangping page puts Zhang Lu in Bazhong only as a retreat when Yangping Pass fell (215) and says nothing of land south of Hanzhong before then ('does not say when or how he gained control'); Guangyuan lies in liu-zhang's Sichuan, which held Yi Province to 214. The circle is also cut at the Sichuan border (about 19 of its 141 cells lay in liu-zhang's admin1).

A 60 km circle at Bazhong (a name the gazetteer lacks) stands for it.

ledger.note: 194: Zhang Lu holds Hanzhong. 'After the success of the rebellion in 194, they founded the theocratic state of Zhang Han in the Hanzhong Valley of Sichuan, enjoying full independence' (Celestial Masters page); Liu Yan had sent Zhang Lu and Zhang Xiu against the Han administrator Su Gu, Zhang Lu killed Zhang Xiu and 'renamed the region Hanning' (Zhang Lu page, no years).

region.text: Bazhong, where Zhang Lu 'retreated' when Yangping Pass was taken and from which he came out to surrender (Battle of Yangping page)

ledger.note: 215: PAGE SILENT on the date and on how Zhang Lu held Bazhong. 'Zhang Lu retreated to Bazhong' when he 'heard that Yangping Pass had been taken' (the pass was reached between 13 August and 10 September 215), and 'led his followers out of Bazhong' to surrender between 9 December 215 and 6 January 216. Yi Province was Liu Bei's by 214, so shu-han (ea-03, not yet written) is entered as the counterpart; the page does not say who held Bazhong before.

ledger.note: 215: Cao Cao's campaign reaches Zhang Lu's land. 'Sometime between 17 April and 15 May 215, Cao Cao launched a campaign against Zhang Lu in Hanzhong Commandery' and 'between 13 August and 10 September 215, Cao Cao's forces reached Yangping Pass' (month 8 used: the first half of that window; the campaign itself was launched in April-May and the page dates no fighting at Yangping, only 'roughly April 215 to January 216' overall).

ledger.note: 215: Zhang Lu surrenders. 'Between 9 December 215 and 6 January 216, Zhang Lu led his followers out of Bazhong and came to surrender to Cao Cao' (Battle of Yangping); the Celestial Masters page: 'In 215, Zhang Lu submitted to Cao Cao'.

region.text: the theocratic state of Hanzhong ('Hanning'): a 100 km circle round Hanzhong, cut at the Sichuan border so that liu-zhang's Yi Province (Sichuan, Chongqing, 188-214) is not drawn twice

ledger.note: 215: Hanzhong passes to Cao Cao. Cao Cao's army 'occupied Nanzheng', the capital, and 'the people in Hanzhong surrendered to Cao Cao, who then renamed the place to Hanzhong from its previous name Hanning'; Xiahou Yuan was left to guard it in January-February 216. Liu Bei, who had seized Yi Province, 'occupied Bazhong after Zhang Lu left' (undated).

region.text: Bazhong, where Zhang Lu 'retreated' when Yangping Pass was taken and from which he came out to surrender (Battle of Yangping page)

ledger.note: 215: the Hanzhong state ends. Zhang Lu was appointed General Who Guards the South by Cao Cao (Zhang Lu page); his followers were resettled 'to the Chang'an area' and 'to Luoyang' (Celestial Masters page, undated). The land left at the end is the Bazhong refuge; Liu Bei 'occupied Bazhong after Zhang Lu left' (undated), see successors.

notes:
Zhang Lu, the Hanzhong theocracy 194-215. 3 pages opened (Zhang Lu (Han dynasty), Way of the Celestial Masters, Battle of Yangping); no Cliopatria row.
Unsettled: (1) the Zhang Lu page gives no years; 194 is the Celestial Masters page's ('After the success of the rebellion in 194'); (2) the Zhang Lu page says Zhang Lu 'nominally followed the orders of Liu Yan' and was recognised by the court, so he could be drawn as a Han vassal rather than independent: recorded as independent (the Celestial Masters page: 'enjoying full independence'); (3) the extent beyond Hanzhong Commandery and the Bazhong refuge is not on any page (the End of the Han page says only 'Hanzhong'); (4) the surrender range 9 December 215 - 6 January 216 straddles the year line: 215 month 12 used, and the End of the Han page's 'January 216' for the Cao Cao handover is noted but not used; (5) when Liu Bei occupied Bazhong is undated.
Counterparts: han-dynasty, cao-cao, shu-han exist or are in ea-03; liu-zhang (Yi Province) is written by this batch.
Gazetteer names needed: Bazhong (city in Sichuan) is used only in text; Guangyuan stands for it.
Repair pass (ea-02-x-fixed): (1) the Guangyuan 80 km circle is removed from 194-214 (it lay in liu-zhang's Sichuan and the opened pages put Zhang Lu in Bazhong only in 215); the Hanzhong circle is cut at the Sichuan border. (2) Bazhong is kept as a 215 refuge (keyframe zhang-lu_215, a gain at confidence 1 and the dissolve region) with the place name 'Bazhong', which the gazetteer lacks (modern prefecture-level city in north-eastern Sichuan); counterpart shu-han is ea-03's and not yet written. (3) contest_start month 8 is the first half of the page's 13 August-10 September window for reaching Yangping Pass; the April-May launch is the campaign's start, not a contest, and the fighting at Yangping is undated; confidence 2.
